problems.stem: An online course consists entirely of recorded videos plus end-of-module multiple-choice quizzes. Which Moore interactions are present?
options: All three interaction types are present.
Only learner-content interaction; learner-instructor and learner-learner interactions are missing or incidental.
problems.explanation: Recorded videos plus auto-graded quizzes are pure learner-content. Strong online courses deliberately add the other two interaction types.

problems.stem: A discussion forum produces lots of messages but the conversation never moves past sharing examples and articles. Which phase of cognitive presence is the course failing to reach?
options: Integration and resolution; the discourse is stuck at exploration and never synthesizes or commits to a defensible answer.
All four phases are equally present.
problems.explanation: The four-phase cognitive presence sequence requires moving past exploration into integration and resolution. Stalling at exploration is one of the most common online-learning defects.

problems.stem: Which scenario most justifies a synchronous (real-time) session over an asynchronous one?
options: Letting learners read a complex paper at their own pace.
A real-time discourse session where learners must respond to each other's reasoning as it unfolds, with the instructor surfacing tensions in the moment.
Recording a one-way 90-minute lecture for later viewing.
problems.explanation: Synchronous time is most valuable for live discourse and immediate feedback that asynchronous mode cannot reproduce. One-way lectures or self-paced reading should be asynchronous.

problems.stem: Teaching presence in the Community of Inquiry framework is best described as:
options: The instructor showing their face on camera.
The design and direction of the educational experience: course architecture, facilitation of discourse, and direct instruction.
Posting more content than learners can read.
problems.explanation: Teaching presence is the design-and-facilitation function. Camera presence is one expression of it but not the construct.
